A maintenance release with two changes you will actually notice: `get_floors`
answers with less by default, and the extension now requires Node 22. No tool was
added or removed — the server still declares 109.

## `get_floors` returns the totals, not the whole day

`get_floors` always returned the 96 quarter-hour intervals behind a day's totals,
whether or not anyone wanted them. That is roughly 5600 characters of response to
answer "how many floors did I climb today", and every one of them lands in the
model's context.

The daily totals now come back on their own, around 210 characters. The breakdown
is still there when it is the point of the question:

```
get_floors(date: "2026-08-22", includeBreakdown: true)
```

Ask for it when you want to know *when* during the day the climbing happened.
Leave it off for everything else.

## Node 22 is now the minimum

The manifest asked for Node 18. That version stopped receiving security patches on
30 April 2025, and Node 20 followed on 30 April 2026 — so the extension was
advertising two runtimes that no longer get fixed. It now asks for Node 22,
supported until April 2027.

Nothing in the server needed changing to suit it: the code only uses long-standing
APIs. This is a declaration catching up with reality rather than a port.

**If you are on Node 18 or 20**, Claude Desktop will now consider the extension
incompatible. Updating Node is the fix, and it is worth doing regardless — those
releases no longer receive security patches of their own.

That floor was written in two places, `package.json` and the manifest, and nothing
compared them. They could drift apart and only an MCP Directory review would find
out. CI now checks them against each other, and builds on both ends of the
supported range instead of only the newest.

## Security

Every open advisory in the dependency tree is closed. `npm audit` reports nothing.

| Package | Was | Now | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hono` | 4.12.31 | 4.13.3 | Four advisories: SSR output retained across requests, DoS in the Language middleware, ReDoS in CORS, `Connection` headers not stripped |
| `fast-uri` | 4.1.1 | 4.1.2 | Host confusion via a backslash authority introducer |
| `ip-address` | 10.2.0 | 10.5.0 | Reached through the SDK's rate limiter |
| `tmp` | 0.0.33 | 0.2.7 | Symlink and path-traversal writes. Build-time only, through the bundle packer |

Two of these were the same mistake in different places: the version floor pinned
in `overrides` had been correct when it was written and was never raised when the
next advisory landed, so npm settled on a version below the fix. `hono` and
`fast-uri` both sat one patch short.

`hono` was not reachable in the shipped server, which talks over stdio and never
imports it — but it travels inside the bundle, so the floor is worth holding.

## Also updated

`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.29.0 → 1.30.0, `axios` 1.18.1 → 1.19.0.

## Install

Download `garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb` and open it with Claude Desktop, or drag it onto
Settings → Extensions. Verify the download first:

```
sha256sum -c garmin-mcp-ts.mcpb.sha256
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/sedoglia/garmin-mcp-ts/compare/v4.3.3...v4.4.0
